description: R-PAR-1 PAR-FOLD, SQL-AGG-ORDER: What do partial sums of the large FL witness give: Sum for g3 over all rows, over d = 1, d <> 1, d > 1 and d < 0; for g1, g2 and g3 over the lower and the upper part of the id range (g1 at id 2049, g2 at id 6000, g3 at id 10000); and Sum of the two partial sums of g1, g2 and g3 (d = 1 part and the rest) through UNION ALL in both arm orders? Runs on a fresh copy of r-par-1-fold2 opened read-only through DAO OpenDatabase in one process and one STA; each statement is opened with Database.OpenRecordset as a snapshot unless stated, and every call's result, HRESULT and DBEngine.Errors are captured.

args.text: SELECT Sum(d) AS s FROM FL WHERE g = 3
SELECT Sum(d) AS s FROM FL WHERE g = 3 AND d = 1
SELECT Sum(d) AS s FROM FL WHERE g = 3 AND d <> 1
SELECT Sum(d) AS s FROM FL WHERE g = 3 AND d > 1
SELECT Sum(d) AS s FROM FL WHERE g = 3 AND d < 0
SELECT Sum(d) AS s FROM FL WHERE g = 1 AND id <= 2049
SELECT Sum(d) AS s FROM FL WHERE g = 1 AND id > 2049
SELECT Sum(d) AS s FROM FL WHERE g = 2 AND id <= 6000
SELECT Sum(d) AS s FROM FL WHERE g = 2 AND id > 6000
SELECT Sum(d) AS s FROM FL WHERE g = 3 AND id <= 10000
SELECT Sum(d) AS s FROM FL WHERE g = 3 AND id > 10000
SELECT Sum(s) AS total FROM (SELECT Sum(d) AS s FROM FL WHERE g = 1 AND d = 1 UNION ALL SELECT Sum(d) AS s FROM FL WHERE g = 1 AND d <> 1)
SELECT Sum(s) AS total FROM (SELECT Sum(d) AS s FROM FL WHERE g = 1 AND d <> 1 UNION ALL SELECT Sum(d) AS s FROM FL WHERE g = 1 AND d = 1)
SELECT Sum(s) AS total FROM (SELECT Sum(d) AS s FROM FL WHERE g = 2 AND d = 1 UNION ALL SELECT Sum(d) AS s FROM FL WHERE g = 2 AND d <> 1)
SELECT Sum(s) AS total FROM (SELECT Sum(d) AS s FROM FL WHERE g = 2 AND d <> 1 UNION ALL SELECT Sum(d) AS s FROM FL WHERE g = 2 AND d = 1)
SELECT Sum(s) AS total FROM (SELECT Sum(d) AS s FROM FL WHERE g = 3 AND d = 1 UNION ALL SELECT Sum(d) AS s FROM FL WHERE g = 3 AND d <> 1)
SELECT Sum(s) AS total FROM (SELECT Sum(d) AS s FROM FL WHERE g = 3 AND d <> 1 UNION ALL SELECT Sum(d) AS s FROM FL WHERE g = 3 AND d = 1)
